correctness.rationale: From |cos theta+ia sin theta|^2=1+(a^2-1)sin^2 theta, rebuilt the exact Gaussian norm integral. For c<1 the e^{-(1-c)x^2} global majorant proves norm and TV limit. At c=1, x=n^{1/4}u yields quartic limit -u^4/2 and integrable upper bound; integral equals 2^{-3/4}Gamma(1/4)/sqrt(pi). For c>1, global comparison -y²+log(1+cy²) has precisely two maximizers ±sqrt((c-1)/c), I(c)=log c-1+1/c; independently expanded the O(1/n) exponent q(y)=-cy^4/[3(1+cy²)] giving claimed nontrivial prefactor and weak two-peak limit. All limits are for fixed c and do not imply uniform crossover.
